title: Mate with the Rook
subtitle: One rook, one king, and a box that keeps shrinking.
goals: Cut the enemy king off with the rook
Bring your own king up to take the escape squares
Finish with the rook check along the edge

steps.say: King and rook against a lone king. It is a forced win every time, and it takes about fifteen moves — but only if you use both pieces. The rook alone can never mate; the king alone can never mate. The method is a box: the rook draws a line the enemy king may not cross, your king walks up, and the box gets one rank smaller at a time.
Watch the box shrink. Notice that the rook only ever checks when the check gains a rank — otherwise it is your KING that does the work.

autoMoves.say: First, bring the king. A rook on its own just chases the enemy king in circles.
Now a useful check: the black king is pushed off the fifth rank, and the rook on a5 becomes a fence it can never cross.
King up again. The box is now ranks 6-8 — three ranks instead of eight.
Marching toward the opposition. The kings will end up facing each other with one square between them — that is the trigger for the next check.
There it is: kings in opposition, so the check shrinks the box again. Ranks 7-8 left.
And the process repeats until the black king is on the last rank with your king opposite. Same idea, every time: king up, wait for the opposition, then check.

steps.prompt: The black king is on the last rank and your king is close. Finish it — mate in two.
hints: Don't check yet. Move your king so the black king has exactly one square left.
Kf7! covers g8 and g7, so Black is forced to h7 — and then the rook checks along the file the king is standing on.
Kf7 Kh7, and now Rh1 is mate.

line.say: The waiting move that does everything. g8 and g7 are now covered by your king, so the black king has exactly one legal square.

Mate. Here is the detail worth learning: the king cannot run to h8, because h8 is on the same file as the checking rook — the moment the king steps off h7, the rook's line reaches h8 too. A king can never escape a rook check by moving ALONG the line of the check.

rejections.say: Check for the sake of check. The black king simply walks to h7 and you have made no progress — worse, you've given up the rook's ideal square. Bring the KING first: it must take away g7 and g8.
Close, and it stalemates you out of a win: from g6 your king covers g7 and h7, and the black king on h8 would have no legal move at all. Step to f7 instead, leaving Black exactly one square.
Premature. With your king still on f6, the black king answers Kg8 and slips away toward the centre. Take g8 away first with Kf7.
A waiting move with the wrong piece. Your rook is already perfectly placed to swing to the h-file; it's the king that needs one more step.

steps.wrongSay: Before you check, ask how many squares the black king has. If it has two, a check just lets it run. Make it one.
steps.successSay: King first, rook last. Every basic mate in chess works the same way — the big piece delivers, but the king does the cornering.
